page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc9ae.48xlarge is a dedicated bare-metal server configured for large-scale compute workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates AMD EPYC 9T95 processors running at 2.25 GHz, delivering 192 dedicated vCPUs. The server pairs this processing capacity with 384 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This 1:2 memory-to-compute ratio prioritizes raw compute density and multithreaded processing capacity. The bare-metal design leverages KVM virtualization mechanisms without sharing physical CPU resources across tenants.

The instance provision contains zero integrated local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring an explicit GPU count of zero. Consequently, all persistent state and operating system files must be deployed on network-attached storage architectures. To support substantial input and output communication, the server provides a robust 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This high-throughput network fabric accommodates high-frequency storage calls and cluster synchronization, offsetting the lack of onboard NVMe drives while facilitating distributed cluster integration.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, provisioning bare-metal hardware with a dense 192-core allocation reduces overhead costs associated with managing multiple smaller virtualized instances. Organizations gain predictable, unthrottled CPU performance across all available threads. The server is well matched for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive per-core memory, including large-scale software compilation, distributed simulations, batch video encoding, continuous integration pipelines, and parallel data transformations within cluster frameworks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc9ae.48xlarge is a high-density bare-metal instance within the ECS Bare Metal family, engineered for parallel compute-intensive tasks. Driven by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T95 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz, the system exposes 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384 GB of system memory. With a 1:2 memory-to-core allocation (2.0 GB per vCPU), its resource balance aligns directly with compute-dominated applications rather than large memory caching layers. The platform lacks bundled local disk storage and includes no integrated GPUs, requiring all persistent storage to rely on external network-attached volumes. For network data transfers, the instance delivers a 100 Gbps baseline throughput, supporting heavy inter-node communication across distributed clusters. By removing hypervisor-level CPU contention, the bare-metal profile maximizes resource efficiency for scalable enterprise software builds, video rendering, scientific modeling, ETL processing, and massive batch simulation workloads.
